occurrences.snippet: Just as the Gītā of Kṛṣṇa, lord of yoga, is dear to people, so the Kṛṣṇā flute is dear to those who have faith in music.

occurrences.subsection_title: The Kinds of Flute and Suitable Materials
occurrences.snippet: Hence the flute is seen in the world in three kinds, resting on the three guṇas; their names are Tripurā, Kṛṣṇā and Jihvāvatī.

occurrences.subsection_title: The Kinds of Flute and Suitable Materials
occurrences.snippet: Thus three kinds of flute, the gift of three ages and based on the three guṇas, are mainly in use today. Their names are Tripurā (the flute blown from the bamboo's natural opening)…
Three kinds of flute are chiefly recognised: the Jihvāvatī and the Kṛṣṇā, and the third is the Prākṛtī.
That is, by [the kind of] mukharandhra (mouth-hole) the flute is of three main kinds. Their names in order are: (1) Jihvāvatī (fipple flute) (2) Kṛṣṇā (transverse flute) (3) Prākṛt…

The Kṛṣṇā was made by Kṛṣṇa, the author of the Gītā and the great yogī; at the start it is hard to master, but in the end it gives joy.
That is, the Kṛṣṇā flute was made by Lord Yogeśvara Śrī Kṛṣṇa. So it has only this much fault, that at the start one has to practise it with hardship, and so some people grow weary…
